entries.original:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

entries.correspondence: Parameters n,m are natural dimensions, u is the total representative of the original positive-time map, and q is the fixed Euclidean vector. H001 retains n,m≥1 and joint smoothness precisely on the open positive-time domain; H002 retains ‖q‖=1; H003 is unit length at every spatial point and positive time. H004 retains a pointwise existential real scalar multiplying u, with the componentwise Laplacian as the finite sum of second derivatives and no regularity of a. H005 retains a common compact spatial set for each closed interval 0<s<t (without requiring uniqueness), uniformly for all its times and outside spatial points. Restricting any such total u to positive time gives the original data; conversely any original map extends by q at nonpositive times, and local equality on the open domain preserves all derivatives and these assumptions. The standard basis Fin n is a coordinate relabeling and the Euclidean norm gives exactly the Frobenius sum of spatial squares, with no factor 1/2. WME is the specified density on positive time and WMEnergy its volume integral; the integrability conjunct ensures this is the actual finite Lebesgue integral. For every t>0, HasDerivAt (WMEnergy u) 0 t is equivalent to differentiability and deriv (WMEnergy u) t=0, by uniqueness and the derivative of a differentiable real function. Ordinary differentiation of the total energy at t agrees in both directions with differentiation on the original open positive-time interval, since a neighborhood of t stays positive. No assertion at t=0 or negative times is made, and no extra hypothesis is added by the representation. E004 remains the declared foundation premise; all retained M ports are discharged from Mathlib in the export.
